MiMedx Group, FY ending 2012-12-31. Management says: Financing cash flow decrease due to lower warrant/option exercises and Surgical Biologics acquisition payment (E30)
Numbers show: Describes financing cash flow components; does not address operating cash flow or receivables per E30
Fit in sample 1: fits. Evidence: E30.
Questions for management: What drove the 248.6% revenue growth (organic demand, acquisitions, channel loading, pricing)? Why did receivables grow 304.5% vs 248.6% revenue growth, pushing DSO from 89 to 103 days? What specific changes in credit terms, customer mix, or shipment timing explain the receivables buildup? Why did operating cash flow improve less than net income (CFO -$3.4M vs NI -$7.7M in 2012)? Were there changes in payment terms, channel stuffing, or revenue recognition timing that contributed to the revenue and receivables patterns? What were the primary drivers of the 248.6% revenue increase (e.g., volume, price, new products, acquisitions, channel loading)? Why did receivables grow 304.5% versus 248.6% revenue growth, and why did DSO increase from 89 to 103 days (e.g., longer payment terms, shipment timing, customer mix)? What specific working-capital or non-cash items drove the $3.3M improvement in operating cash flow despite continued net losses and a large receivables build? What specific demand drivers (new products, market expansion, pricing, acquisitions) caused the 248.6% revenue increase? Why did receivables grow 304.5% vs 248.6% revenue growth, pushing DSO from 89 to 103 days — was this due to longer payment terms, channel loading, shipment timing, or collection issues? What portion of the revenue growth came from the Surgical Biologics acquisition (referenced in E30 as a $427K financing outflow), and what was the acquired revenue contribution? Why did operating cash flow remain negative (-$3.4M) despite $19.3M incremental revenue? What working capital changes (receivables, inventory, payables) drove the gap? Can you provide quarterly revenue and receivables data to assess whether Q4 shipment timing or channel loading inflated year-end receivables?
